title: Японцы отказались от рыбы  (The Japanese Refuse the Fish)

segments.t: Waiters carry all the fish dishes back to the kitchen because the Japanese delegation immediately smelled that the fish wasn't fresh. Mikhail Jekovich deducts the cost from the cooks' wages, and Senya stubbornly eats a piece to prove them wrong.
Потому что она совсем не свежая.
Стоимость блюд я вычту у вас.
Не надо моих гостей кормить этим.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'The waiters are carrying your fish back.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'waiters' before landing on 'are carrying'.
'The Japanese refused to eat this fish.' Notice how Russian expresses 'Japanese man' and 'fish' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Потому что она совсем не свежая.
'Because it is not fresh at all.' Mikhail anchors the line on 'that is why', while 'fresh' completes the thought.
Стоимость блюд я вычту у вас.
'I will deduct the cost of the dishes from you.' Notice how Russian expresses 'cost' and 'you' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Wow, that is quite a fine.' The meaning hinges on 'nothing' working together with 'fine' in spoken Russian.
Не надо моих гостей кормить этим.
'Do not feed my guests with this.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'to feed' to negate the statement. Senya answers right away.
'By the way, this is very tasty fish.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'by the way' and finishing on 'fish'.
'The Japanese simply do not understand anything.' In Russian, the idea of 'Japanese man' flows naturally into 'to understand' without extra filler words.
'Well, how do you like our fish?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'fish'. Senya answers right away.
'The discounted fish went down well!' Notice how Russian expresses 'fish' and 'am off' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Senya, what is wrong with you right now?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Senya' before landing on 'now'.

'I need to step out urgently for a minute.' The grammar packs 'to me' and 'a minute' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Потому что она совсем не свежая.
Стоимость блюд я вычту у вас.
Не надо моих гостей кормить этим.
Senya's stomach immediately rebels against the bargain fish, while Mikhail sneaks his pony inside the hotel for the night. Until next time!
